question.worked_solution:
The sum and constant multiple rules for double summations state that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}({a}_{ij}+{b}_{ij}) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{a}_{ij}+{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{b}_{ij}, \\ {\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}k{a}_{ij} & =k{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{a}_{ij}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying these rules to the given sum, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{50}{\sum }_{j=1}^{100}4({a}_{ij}+{b}_{ij}) & =4{\sum }_{i=1}^{50}{\sum }_{j=1}^{100}({a}_{ij}+{b}_{ij}) \\  & =4{\sum }_{i=1}^{50}{\sum }_{j=1}^{100}{a}_{ij}+4{\sum }_{i=1}^{50}{\sum }_{j=1}^{100}{b}_{ij} \\  & =4\cdot 40+4\cdot 60 \\  & =160+240 \\  & =400.\end{aligned}
$$
